headline: Zya raises $15M for drop-in sugar reduction; coffee-ground and olive cocoa substitutes
summary: Zya closed a $15M Series A for a technology that turns sugar into fibre after eating without reformulation, with multinationals moving to co-development, making it a partnership target for sugar-reduced Patisserie and Belcolade lines.

Cocoa substitutes keep multiplying: RFINE's KAFFIKA upcycles coffee grounds into a cocoa alternative and Kansas State/Pelotas showed olive pomace flour can replace 25% of cocoa powder in muffins with no consumer penalty.
Biotech routes to cocoa supply are gaining attention as bean shortages persist, worth tracking as a long-term Belcolade hedge.
Avebe's cold-activated PuraMYL 440 potato starch builds texture without heating, a quick test candidate for cold-process creams and fillings.
On the regulatory side, Uttar Pradesh is cracking down on labels that imply ingredients present only as flavour or toppings, a reminder for chocolate- and fruit-flavoured product claims in India.

items.title: Upcycled Cocoa Alternative Ingredients: RFINE KAFFIKA Turns Coffee Grounds Into Cocoa…
items.summary: RFINE's KAFFIKA is an upcycled cocoa alternative made from spent coffee grounds.
items.why: A ready-to-test cocoa-powder alternative for chocolate-flavoured fillings, coatings and bakery could cut cocoa exposure; evaluate as a supplier or partner.

items.title: Chocolate-making cocoa beans are increasingly in short supply. There may be a biotech fix
items.summary: Genetic Literacy Project article on biotech approaches (such as gene editing or cell culture) to address shrinking cocoa bean supply.
items.why: Biotech cocoa routes are a direct long-run supply hedge for Belcolade; keep tracking the companies behind them as partner or competitor candidates.

items.title: Exclusive: Zya raises $15m Series A to rethink sugar reduction, no reformulation required
items.summary: Zya raised a $15M Series A for a sugar-reduction technology that converts sugar into fibre after eating, without reformulation; it has feasibility projects with multinationals heading to co-development.
items.why: A drop-in sugar-reduction approach for sweet goods, fillings and chocolate makes Zya a strong partnership target for Patisserie and Belcolade.

items.title: Zya raises $15M Series A to turn sugar into fibre after you eat
items.summary: Dealroom report on Zya's $15M Series A to turn sugar into fibre in the gut after consumption.
items.why: Same Zya deal: a co-development candidate for sugar-reduced Patisserie and chocolate without reformulation.

items.title: Olive Pomace Flour as a Partial Cocoa Replacer in Chocolate Muffins: Expanding the Potential of a By-Product
items.summary: Brazilian and Kansas State researchers replaced 25% of cocoa powder in chocolate muffins with olive pomace flour, with no loss in volume, texture or consumer acceptance.
items.why: A low-cost, upcycled partial cocoa-powder replacer for chocolate cakes and muffins could ease cocoa cost pressure in Patisserie mixes; worth a pilot or contact with Kansas State.

items.title: How Fiber Can Rule in a Clean Label World
items.summary: Sponsored piece on 1:1 high-fibre flour swaps to add fibre to clean-label bakery products.
items.why: High-fibre flour swaps compete with or complement Puratos fibre-enrichment solutions for clean-label bread.

items.why: Treated, safer flour is increasingly relevant for ready-to-eat applications and fillings; track the mill's process as a supplier benchmark.

items.title: Cold-Activated Potato Starches: Avebe PuraMYL 440 Builds Food Texture Without Heating
items.summary: Avebe launched PuraMYL 440, a cold-activated potato starch that builds texture without heating.
items.why: A cold-set clean-label starch is directly usable in instant creams, fillings and toppings; test it for Patisserie cold-process products.

items.why: Background content on yeast's role in quality; useful context for Bakery's yeast and fermentation messaging.

items.title: Antidiabetic potential of cocoa bean shell extract (Theobroma Cacao L.): phytochemical profile, α-glucosidase inhibition and ex vivo GLP-1 secretion

items.title: HPLC and LC-MS/MS analysis of intermediate wheatgrass protein composition.
items.summary: University of Manitoba analysis shows intermediate wheatgrass (Kernza) lacks key high-molecular-weight glutenin subunits, explaining its weak gluten network.
items.why: Perennial grains are a sustainability theme for bread; understanding their gluten gaps points to enzyme/improver solutions Puratos could offer.
